gap: No validated agency-transfer construct or profile
why_material: Without construct validity, policy cannot distinguish strong assistance, legitimate persuasion, process manipulation, delegation, dependence, and concentrated control.
current_evidence: Adjacent evidence covers persuasion, overreliance, sycophancy, switching and concentration, but not a general cumulative construct.
needed_study_artifact: Develop a six-axis Agency Transfer Profile: process integrity; decision displacement; reflective endorsement/contestability; delegation scope; dependence/path dependence; concentration/exposure. Validate reliability and discriminant/predictive validity; do not aggregate prematurely.
decision_enabled: Impact-assessment module, longitudinal monitoring and sharper claims—not a legal threshold by itself.

gap: No valid evidence chain from model signal to deployment gate
why_material: APE and MASK measure persuasive attempts and honesty under pressure, not causal human harm; a benchmark cutoff would create false precision.
current_evidence: Provider frameworks and GPAI duties use multiple evaluations, exposure and residual risk; no common manipulation score-to-release threshold exists.
needed_study_artifact: Validate T0–T3 evidence tiers: signal; system risk; context-specific deployment gate; post-market trigger. Predeclare human outcomes, uncertainty, exposure and domain-specific smallest effects of interest.
decision_enabled: Mitigation, affordance limits or staged access in a defined context; never automatic prohibition from APE/MASK alone.
likely_owner: AI Office; safety institutes; independent labs

gap: No compositional-safety standard for multi-agent workflows
why_material: Local safeguards can pass while the global workflow creates harm.
current_evidence: Agent standards work and security authorization precedents.
needed_study_artifact: Root-purpose schemas, adversarial task decomposition, global-guard trials, and auditability tests.

gap: Longitudinal, relational and memory-mediated evidence is thin
why_material: The central hypothesis concerns cumulative trust, path dependence and reduced reversibility, while most evidence is short and task-bounded.
current_evidence: Short persuasion studies; limited four-week observational/experimental evidence; task-specific offloading and one-interaction sycophancy effects.
needed_study_artifact: Factorial memory × conflict × disclosure studies; ethically controlled follow-up with cooling-off, counterevidence, washout, unassisted performance, switching and recovery.
decision_enabled: User memory/exit controls now; loyalty, dependency and vulnerability duties only after causal validation.

gap: No evidence base for a general open-weight release gate
why_material: Irreversible release reduces monitoring and withdrawal, but blanket licensing can entrench closed incumbents and push activity offshore.
current_evidence: Systemic-risk duties can apply to open models, yet EU law has no capability-based prior approval to publish weights; derivative visibility is fragmented.
needed_study_artifact: Compare release modalities using capability, modifiability, reach, reversibility, safeguards, derivative coverage, misuse and market effects; test safe harbours.
decision_enabled: Context-specific safety cases, staged access pilots and repository metadata—not a presumed general licence.
likely_owner: AI institutes; repositories; model providers; competition experts

gap: Local-language, vulnerable-group, and Global South evidence gap
why_material: Manipulation, trust, and election administration are culturally and linguistically specific.
current_evidence: Benchmarks and studies skew toward English and high-resource settings.
needed_study_artifact: Locally governed evaluations with representative recruitment, language experts, and election authorities.

gap: Organic, proxy, and conversational influence escapes political-ad definitions
why_material: Sponsor and targeting rules can be avoided without buying a formally classified ad.
current_evidence: Ad repositories and sponsor duties cover defined paid advertising.
needed_study_artifact: Audit proxy sponsors, affiliate steering, issue advocacy, and assistant recommendations.
decision_enabled: Conflict, disclosure, and targeting rules based on function rather than format.

why_material: Privacy-preserving systems provide limited visibility into repeated forwarding and migration.
current_evidence: Aggregate forwarding controls and incident reports in some jurisdictions.
needed_study_artifact: Privacy-preserving aggregate exposure indicators and cross-platform incident protocols.
decision_enabled: Targeted friction and correction without mass surveillance.

gap: Provenance effectiveness under transformation and real user conditions
why_material: Cryptographic credentials can be stripped and visible labels can be ignored or weaponized.
current_evidence: Technical standards and laboratory detection tests.
needed_study_artifact: Transformation robustness, comprehension, correction, and adversarial laundering studies.
decision_enabled: When provenance is sufficient and when other controls are required.

gap: No accepted metric for assistant gatekeeping and epistemic concentration
why_material: Market share misses source selection, omission, answer defaults, and delegated search decisions.
current_evidence: Recommender and media-pluralism metrics are imperfect analogues.
needed_study_artifact: Source concentration, omission, user-control, default, and delegated-decision measures.
decision_enabled: DMA designation, pluralism duties, and interoperability remedies.

gap: Institutional dependence and deskilling are under-measured
why_material: Procurement can silently transfer public judgment and continuity to vendors.
current_evidence: Registers, impact assessments, and switching rules record systems but not lost capability.
needed_study_artifact: Exit exercises, internal skill audits, decision-authority mapping, and outage simulations.

gap: Weak evidence that interventions preserve agency or democratic outcomes
why_material: Compliance plans, labels, takedowns and virality are not equivalent to preserved deliberation, trust or legitimate elections.
current_evidence: Operational metrics and selected experiments; causal election effects are rare and post-hoc attribution is fragile.
needed_study_artifact: Pre-register Brazil 2026 implementation measures before plan submission and voting: exposure, latency, correction overlap, appeals, rights costs, process tracing and bounded quasi-experimental analyses.
decision_enabled: Scale, modify or sunset controls based on implementation and mechanism evidence without claiming that AI changed the election result.

gap: Independent evaluators lack timely access, compute, and publication freedom
why_material: Provider-controlled evidence creates epistemic dependence and selective disclosure.
current_evidence: DSA data access and voluntary lab access with delays and scope limits.
needed_study_artifact: Compare access models; fund secure public compute; measure finding suppression and replication.
decision_enabled: Access rights, levy design, and evaluator accreditation.

gap: Rights and proportionality costs are rarely evaluated alongside mitigation benefit
why_material: Overbroad controls can chill political speech, privacy, dissent, satire, and beneficial openness.
current_evidence: General rights doctrines and platform appeal processes.
needed_study_artifact: Joint risk-rights evaluation with subgroup error, appeal, and chilling-effect measures.
decision_enabled: Narrow triggers, safeguards, sunset clauses, and remedy design.

gap: No threshold for democratic or constitutional significance of an AI assistant
why_material: High-reach assistants can become de facto infrastructure without formal authorization.
current_evidence: Gatekeeper, media, public-law, and treaty analogies.
needed_study_artifact: Measure delegated decisions, reach, default status, institutional dependence, and opinion-formation role.
decision_enabled: Designation, public authorization, heightened duties, or sunset review.

gap: System-level steering audits do not establish human uptake
why_material: Models can hide conflicts or change recommendations under sponsorship, but policy needs to know whether people follow, resist or reverse those recommendations.
current_evidence: Emerging model audits and short human experiments; limited evidence linking conflicted steering to real consequential choice.
needed_study_artifact: Factor conflict × disclosure × memory × personalization; measure recommendation divergence, revealed action, welfare, override, counterevidence response and follow-up.
decision_enabled: Whether to impose a loyalty/conflict duty, disclosure, non-profiling mode or product restriction.
likely_owner: Consumer and competition regulators; independent human-subjects labs
